title: Runtime kernel decision distillation and safety fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: build and validate a compact decision model that distills signals from our existing ensemble of microbenchmarks and online telemetry to pick the best kernel variant per request class, while ensuring a safety fallback that prevents 99.9th percentile latency regressions during rollout. Scope covers prefill vs decode branch decisions, attention kernel variant selection for long context workloads, and interactions with KV cache hit patterns.

Background: we currently run multiple kernel probes and a heuristic selector that uses seqlen and architecture buckets. That approach is accurate but expensive to probe and has brittle edge-cases for mixed prefill/decode bursts. This ticket aims to: 1) aggregate offline microbench and live traces into features, 2) train a distilled decision model (small decision forest or shallow neural net) optimized for inference-time cost, 3) implement a runtime circuit that consults the distilled model and falls back to a conservative kernel on high tail-risk requests, and 4) validate via canary and synthetic traffic stress tests.

Why now: customer workloads with mixed short and long queries are exposing latency tail spikes after recent quantized operator updates. We need a faster, cheaper selector with explicit tail-safety guarantees that plays well with autoscaling and back-pressure policies.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a distilled kernel decision model that reduces per-request probe overhead by >= 60% compared to current ensemble probing in our staging traces
No more than 5% regression in median latency and no more than 3% increase in 99.9th percentile latency across the canary cohort during a 24h canary
Safety fallback path implemented: if runtime telemetry indicates tail-risk (defined in spec), selector uses conservative kernel and emits an alert metric
Unit/integration tests cover decision model inputs, deterministic fallback triggering, and configuration toggles
End-to-end benchmark report with per-model, per-arch, and per-seqlen breakouts in the shared dashboard

implementation_notes: Model format: ONNX or lightgbm binary to be loaded by runtime with deterministic scoring
Feature set must be resilient to missing signals; default values and imputation documented in spec
Fallback definition: conservative kernel is the highest-stability kernel verified across all arch families (pre-computed in kernel catalog)
Telemetry invariants: selector_confidence < 0.2 should increase probe frequency for that cohort to re-label and retrain
Canary plan: rollout to Dedicated pool-B with percentage ramp 1% -> 5% -> 15% over 24h, with automated halt on any 99.9th latency increase > 2% absolute
